findings.explanation: A visitor who is not signed in can read the table "directory", which has no owner column. It may be public on purpose, so the tool cannot tell.
findings.fix: If "directory" should not be public, turn on row security for it and allow reads only for the people who need them. If it is public on purpose, no change is needed.

findings.explanation: A visitor who is not signed in can read the private column "phone" of other people in the table "directory".
findings.fix: Stop visitors and signed-in users from reading "phone" on "directory": take away their read access to the table, then give read access only on the columns that are public. Or move the private column to a separate table that has its own row security policy.
